subject: Mathematics

sections.title: QUESTION 1: EUCLIDEAN GEOMETRY
sections.instructions: Use Source 1. Give reasons for all geometrical statements.

questions.question: Prove that triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC.
memo: Angle ADE = angle ABC and angle AED = angle ACB (corresponding angles, DE || BC).
Therefore triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC (AAA).

questions.question: Hence prove that AD/DB = AE/EC.
memo: AB = AD + DB and AC = AE + EC.
Cross-multiply and cancel AD.AE to obtain AD.EC = AE.DB.

questions.question: Calculate x, the length of EC.
F is the midpoint of AB. A line through F parallel to BC meets AC at G. Prove that G is the midpoint of AC.
memo: AF/FB = 1 because F is the midpoint.
By the proportionality theorem, AF/FB = AG/GC.
Therefore AG/GC = 1, so AG = GC and G is the midpoint of AC.

sections.title: QUESTION 2: REGRESSION AND CORRELATION
sections.instructions: Use Source 2. Round numerical answers to one decimal place where necessary.

questions.question: Describe the direction and strength of the correlation.
Use the regression line to estimate the result for 6.5 hours of study.
Is the estimate in Question 2.3 an interpolation or an extrapolation? Give a reason.
memo: Interpolation, because 6.5 lies within the observed range 2 to 7 hours.

questions.question: Explain why the strong correlation does not by itself prove that extra study time causes higher marks.
memo: Other variables such as prior knowledge, teaching or sleep may influence both variables.
A controlled design or further evidence is needed.

sections.title: QUESTION 3: COUNTING AND PROBABILITY
sections.instructions: Use Source 3 where indicated. Show all probability calculations.
sections.stimulus: Refer to SOURCE 3 for Questions 3.1 to 3.4.

questions.question: Verify that the probabilities on each pair of branches sum to 1.
Calculate the probability that a randomly selected component is defective.
Given that a component is defective, calculate the probability that it came from Line B.
Determine whether the events 'Line B' and 'defective' are independent. Justify your answer.
memo: They are not equal, so the events are not independent.

questions.question: A batch code contains two different letters followed by three digits. Repetition of digits is allowed. How many different codes are possible?
Three components are selected independently from a process with defect probability 0.052. Calculate the probability that at least one is defective.
